# SYMBOL PARITY (Phase A / Phase D)

`nm -D --defined-only` on both shared libraries:

* C:    `c_src/build/libmujs.so`   (cmake, `-w`, default flags)
* Rust: `translation/target/release/libmujs.so` (cdylib)

| metric | value |
|--------|-------|
| dynamic symbols exported by C | 237 |
| dynamic symbols exported by Rust | 237 |
| exported by C but MISSING from Rust | 0 |
| exported by Rust but not by C | 0 |
| undefined non-libc symbols in the Rust .so | 0 |

The symbol diff is EMPTY in both directions. Every remaining undefined symbol of the
Rust `.so` is a libc / libm / libgcc-unwind / glibc-TLS import (`nm -D --undefined-only`
filtered on `@GLIBC|@GCC|_ITM_*|_Unwind_*|__gmon_start__` leaves nothing).

Note: `c_src/CMakeLists.txt` does not link libm, so the C `.so` has undefined `ceil`,
`floor`, `fmod`, ... The test harness dlopens `libm.so.6` with `RTLD_GLOBAL` first, and
keeps both mujs libraries `RTLD_LOCAL` so they can never interpose on each other.

Build/feature matrix: `translation/Cargo.toml` declares NO `[features]` section, so
there is exactly one feature combination (the default = empty). It was verified both
with the default build and with `--no-default-features`.
